name: Meet Your Team
concept: Recognize the goalkeeper and three lines of teammates, then adjust your midfield role as the ball changes sides.
desc: Recognize the goalkeeper and three lines of teammates, then adjust your midfield role as the ball changes sides.

steps.desc: Your team has seven players: one goalkeeper and six outfield players. Attack toward the goal at the far end.
steps.say: Your team has seven players: one goalkeeper and six outfield players. Attack toward the goal at the far end.

steps.desc: Here, two defenders, three midfielders and one forward start ahead of the keeper. That is two-three-one, or one-two-three-one including the keeper.
steps.say: Here, two defenders, three midfielders and one forward start ahead of the keeper. That is two-three-one, or one-two-three-one including the keeper.

steps.desc: The left defender has the ball. The wide midfielder offers a route ahead; the middle midfielder can help from another angle.
steps.say: The left defender has the ball. The wide midfielder offers a route ahead; the middle midfielder can help from another angle.

steps.desc: You are the middle midfielder. Choose a position that gives the left defender another passing angle.
steps.say: You are the middle midfielder. Choose a position that gives the left defender another passing angle.

steps.desc: Move into the inside angle. Your starting position helps you find a job; you can adjust it as play changes.
steps.say: Move into the inside angle. Your starting position helps you find a job; you can adjust it as play changes.

steps.desc: The defender passes inside. The wide player stays available ahead.
steps.say: The defender passes inside. The wide player stays available ahead.

steps.desc: Return the ball. Now watch the defenders move it to the other side.
steps.say: Return the ball. Now watch the defenders move it to the other side.

steps.desc: The right defender receives. The right midfielder offers width, so your supporting job shifts too.
steps.say: The right defender receives. The right midfielder offers width, so your supporting job shifts too.

steps.desc: You are still the middle midfielder. Choose a useful supporting position for the new passer.
steps.say: You are still the middle midfielder. Choose a useful supporting position for the new passer.

steps.desc: Move across to support. The forward stays higher, while the goalkeeper remains available behind the defenders.
steps.say: Move across to support. The forward stays higher, while the goalkeeper remains available behind the defenders.

steps.desc: The pass reaches you. The same team shape helped on both sides because the players adjusted their positions.
steps.say: The pass reaches you. The same team shape helped on both sides because the players adjusted their positions.

steps.desc: The right defender moves up behind the pass. Starting roles help us share jobs as the ball moves.
steps.say: The right defender moves up behind the pass. Starting roles help us share jobs as the ball moves.

catalog.name: Meet Your Team
catalog.what: Recognize the goalkeeper and three lines of teammates, then adjust your midfield role as the ball changes sides.
catalog.coach: Your team has seven players: one goalkeeper and six outfield players. Attack toward the goal at the far end.

questions.q: Where could the middle midfielder help the player with the ball?
questions.explain: The wide midfielder already offers the outside route. An inside position gives the defender a different option.

spots.why: This creates a separate inside passing angle.
This crowds the route already offered by the wide midfielder.

choiceExplanations: This creates a separate inside passing angle.
This crowds the route already offered by the wide midfielder.

questions.q: Where could the middle midfielder help now?
questions.explain: The ball has changed sides. Moving across gives the right defender an inside option alongside the wide teammate.

spots.why: You are farther from the new passer and give them a longer route.
You give the right defender a closer inside option without crowding the wide player.

choiceExplanations: You are farther from the new passer and give them a longer route.
You give the right defender a closer inside option without crowding the wide player.

questions.q: True or false? Your team has two defenders, three midfielders, one forward.
questions.explain: Yes. Two at the back, three in the middle and one ahead, plus the keeper.
choiceExplanations: Yes. Two at the back, three in the middle and one ahead, plus the keeper.
Count again. Two defenders, three midfielders and one forward start ahead of the keeper.

questions.q: The ball goes across the team. Put the steps in order.
options: Left defender passes inside to you
You pass back to the left defender
Ball goes to the right defender
questions.explain: Right. You help, pass back, the ball goes across, then you move across.
choiceExplanations: Right. You help, pass back, the ball goes across, then you move across.
You give it back only after the left defender passes to you.
The ball goes across to the right defender after you pass it back.
You move across once the ball reaches the right defender.

questions.q: The left midfielder has the ball. Where can the middle midfielder help?
questions.explain: Yes. Close and inside gives the passer another angle.
choiceExplanations: That is far from the ball, so the left midfielder has no close help.
Yes. Close and inside gives the passer another angle.
The blue player stands in that lane, so a pass could be cut out.

name: A Formation Gives Us Options
concept: Use the jobs of the back line, midfield and forward to find a missing wide or supporting option.
desc: Use the jobs of the back line, midfield and forward to find a missing wide or supporting option.

steps.desc: A formation is a starting arrangement. Here, one keeper, two defenders, three midfielders and one forward make one-two-three-one.
steps.say: A formation is a starting arrangement. Here, one keeper, two defenders, three midfielders and one forward make one-two-three-one.

steps.desc: The two defenders give support behind midfield. Without the ball, they protect the route to our goal. The keeper helps behind them.
steps.say: The two defenders give support behind midfield. Without the ball, they protect the route to our goal. The keeper helps behind them.

steps.desc: Three midfielders connect the defenders to the forward. Wide players stretch the team; the middle player offers another passing angle.
steps.say: Three midfielders connect the defenders to the forward. Wide players stretch the team; the middle player offers another passing angle.

steps.desc: The forward gives us a target farther up the field. Everyone still moves to help with the ball and to defend without it.
steps.say: The forward gives us a target farther up the field. Everyone still moves to help with the ball and to defend without it.

steps.desc: Look at our right midfielder. They have drifted close to the middle. The passer needs a route on the right.
steps.say: Look at our right midfielder. They have drifted close to the middle. The passer needs a route on the right.

steps.desc: You are the right midfielder. Which move adds the option our shape is missing?
steps.say: You are the right midfielder. Which move adds the option our shape is missing?

steps.desc: Move wide enough to offer a different angle. You can leave your starting spot when the game needs it.
steps.say: Move wide enough to offer a different angle. You can leave your starting spot when the game needs it.

steps.desc: The middle player passes wide. Now the midfield and back line must keep helping the new ball carrier.
steps.say: The middle player passes wide. Now the midfield and back line must keep helping the new ball carrier.

steps.desc: A defender closes the forward route. The middle player has run ahead too, so the ball carrier needs help behind.
steps.say: A defender closes the forward route. The middle player has run ahead too, so the ball carrier needs help behind.

steps.desc: Our forward still offers height. The right defender is deeper; a closer midfield angle can connect the team.
steps.say: Our forward still offers height. The right defender is deeper; a closer midfield angle can connect the team.

steps.desc: You are the middle midfielder now. Which move gives the wide teammate a clear return?
steps.say: You are the middle midfielder now. Which move gives the wide teammate a clear return?

steps.desc: Drop behind and inside. A midfielder can help from different heights as the picture changes.
steps.say: Drop behind and inside. A midfielder can help from different heights as the picture changes.

steps.desc: The return reaches midfield. Width, a player ahead and support behind give the team choices.
steps.say: The return reaches midfield. Width, a player ahead and support behind give the team choices.

steps.desc: One-three-two-one is another possible formation: three defenders, two midfielders and one forward. Neither set of numbers fixes players to the grass.
steps.say: One-three-two-one is another possible formation: three defenders, two midfielders and one forward. Neither set of numbers fixes players to the grass.

steps.desc: Try different positions in practice. Explain who can help ahead, beside and behind you before choosing where to move.
steps.say: Try different positions in practice. Explain who can help ahead, beside and behind you before choosing where to move.

catalog.name: A Formation Gives Us Options
catalog.what: Use the jobs of the back line, midfield and forward to find a missing wide or supporting option.
catalog.coach: A formation is a starting arrangement. Here, one keeper, two defenders, three midfielders and one forward make one-two-three-one.

questions.q: Where would the right midfielder help now?
questions.explain: The left side already has width. Moving right gives the middle player a separate passing route.

spots.why: This restores a wide option on the right.
This crowds midfield and leaves the right side empty.

choiceExplanations: This restores a wide option on the right.
This crowds midfield and leaves the right side empty.

questions.q: Where should the middle midfielder offer support?
questions.explain: The forward option is covered now. A position behind and inside the ball gives the wide player a clear return.

spots.why: This takes you nearer the pressure and leaves no close return.
This links the wide player back to the rest of the team.

choiceExplanations: This takes you nearer the pressure and leaves no close return.
This links the wide player back to the rest of the team.

questions.q: The forward is hiding. Tap where the forward plays.
questions.explain: Yes. The forward gives the team a target farther up the field.
choiceExplanations: That is where the defenders help. The forward gives a target farther up.
Yes. The forward gives the team a target farther up the field.
That is the left midfielder's side. The forward plays up the middle.

questions.q: Which picture gives the wide player a clear pass back?
questions.explain: Yes. Behind and inside gives a short, clear pass back.
choiceExplanations: The middle player is ahead, near a defender, so there is no help behind.
The middle player is too far away, so that pass is long and risky.
Yes. Behind and inside gives a short, clear pass back.

questions.q: Now the left midfielder has drifted inside. Where should they move?
questions.explain: Yes. Wide on the left gives the passer a new route.
choiceExplanations: Yes. Wide on the left gives the passer a new route.
The middle is crowded, and the blue player can block that pass.
That is too close to our defender, so it adds no new route ahead.

name: Goal Kick & Build-Out Line
concept: On our goal kick, the other team waits behind the build-out line. Once the ball is kicked and moves, they can come and press.
desc: On our goal kick, the other team waits behind the build-out line. Once the ball is kicked and moves, they can come and press.

steps.desc: This example uses AYSO build-out rules. Other competitions can use different rules; the shared idea is making room to restart and helping the keeper.
steps.say: This example uses AYSO build-out rules. Other competitions can use different rules; the shared idea is making room to restart and helping the keeper.

steps.desc: Our team has a goal kick. The dashed line across our half sits halfway between the penalty area and the halfway line.
steps.say: Our team has a goal kick. The dashed line across our half sits halfway between the penalty area and the halfway line.

steps.desc: Before this goal kick, where must the blue player move to give our team room?
steps.say: Before this goal kick, where must the blue player move to give our team room?

steps.desc: Blue retreats beyond the line. Our defenders offer routes on either side while the keeper prepares the stationary ball.
steps.say: Blue retreats beyond the line. Our defenders offer routes on either side while the keeper prepares the stationary ball.

steps.desc: A goal kick may go short or beyond the line. Here the left defender is available. Pressure can return once the ball is kicked and clearly moves.
steps.say: A goal kick may go short or beyond the line. Here the left defender is available. Pressure can return once the ball is kicked and clearly moves.

steps.desc: The keeper kicks to the left defender. The ball is now in play; blue does not have to wait for the receiver to touch it.
steps.say: The keeper kicks to the left defender. The ball is now in play; blue does not have to wait for the receiver to touch it.

steps.desc: The kick has been taken. Blue can now cross the line, even though the ball stayed on our side of it.
steps.say: The kick has been taken. Blue can now cross the line, even though the ball stayed on our side of it.

steps.desc: The same blue player has a new choice now. Does the line still keep them back?
steps.say: The same blue player has a new choice now. Does the line still keep them back?

steps.desc: Blue approaches the receiver. Our middle player offers a new angle, because the protected restart has become open play.
steps.say: Blue approaches the receiver. Our middle player offers a new angle, because the protected restart has become open play.

steps.desc: The defender passes to midfield before the pressure arrives. Support must continue after the restart.
steps.say: The defender passes to midfield before the pressure arrives. Support must continue after the restart.

steps.desc: The keeper may also restart quickly before every opponent retreats, accepting the risk of interception. Waiting gives teammates time to find space.
steps.say: The keeper may also restart quickly before every opponent retreats, accepting the risk of interception. Waiting gives teammates time to find space.

steps.desc: With the ball held in the keeper’s hands, AYSO also requires retreat. Release from the hands lets opponents cross; an ordinary pass back in open play does not create that protection.
steps.say: With the ball held in the keeper’s hands, AYSO also requires retreat. Release from the hands lets opponents cross; an ordinary pass back in open play does not create that protection.

steps.desc: In this AYSO profile the far build-out line also changes the offside boundary. This lesson teaches the goal kick; check your competition before applying these rules.
steps.say: In this AYSO profile the far build-out line also changes the offside boundary. This lesson teaches the goal kick; check your competition before applying these rules.

steps.desc: The midfielder carries into the available angle. The left defender moves up behind to stay connected after the restart.
steps.say: The midfielder carries into the available angle. The left defender moves up behind to stay connected after the restart.

catalog.name: Goal Kick & Build-Out Line
catalog.what: On our goal kick, the other team waits behind the build-out line. Once the ball is kicked and moves, they can come and press.
catalog.coach: This example uses AYSO build-out rules. Other competitions can use different rules; the shared idea is making room to restart and helping the keeper.

questions.q: Where must the blue player retreat before the goal kick?
options: Behind the build-out line, toward halfway
questions.explain: For this AYSO goal kick, opponents must retreat behind the build-out line. The ball is still stationary.

spots.why: This is beyond the line, away from the goal being restarted.
This stays inside the protected area and moves closer to the keeper.

choiceExplanations: This is beyond the line, away from the goal being restarted.
This stays inside the protected area and moves closer to the keeper.

questions.q: After the goal kick clearly moves, what may blue do?
options: Stay behind the line until the ball crosses it
Cross the line to approach the ball
questions.explain: Under this AYSO profile, the kicked and clearly moving ball releases the opponents. The receiver does not need to touch it first.

spots.why: Waiting is a tactical choice, but the rule no longer requires it.
Blue may cross now because the goal kick has put the ball in play.

choiceExplanations: Waiting is a tactical choice, but the rule no longer requires it.
Blue may cross now because the goal kick has put the ball in play.

questions.q: True or false? Blue must wait until our defender touches the ball.
questions.explain: Right, it's false. Once the kick moves the ball, blue can press.
choiceExplanations: Blue can come once the kick is taken and the ball moves.
Right, it's false. Once the kick moves the ball, blue can press.

questions.q: A goal kick with the build-out line. Put the steps in order.
options: Blue moves back past the line
Keeper kicks to the left defender
Blue runs in toward our defender
questions.explain: Right. Blue moves back, we kick, blue runs in, so we pass on.
choiceExplanations: Right. Blue moves back, we kick, blue runs in, so we pass on.
The keeper kicks only after blue has moved back past the line.
Blue can only run in after the kick moves the ball.
The defender passes on last, because blue is running in.

questions.q: Before the kick, blue's forward is too close. Where must they go?
questions.explain: Yes. Blue moves past the line, so we have room to restart.
choiceExplanations: That is even closer to our keeper. Blue must give us room.
Standing on the line is not enough. Blue must move past it.
Yes. Blue moves past the line, so we have room to restart.

name: Look, Then Turn or Return
concept: Look for pressure before receiving. Turn into room or give the ball back.
desc: Look for pressure before receiving. Turn into room or give the ball back.

steps.desc: Before the pass arrives, look over your shoulder. Where is the defender?
steps.say: Before the pass arrives, look over your shoulder. Where is the defender?

steps.desc: The pass reaches your feet. Keep your body open so you can see ahead.
steps.say: The pass reaches your feet. Keep your body open so you can see ahead.

steps.desc: There is room in front of you. A small touch can take you into it.
steps.say: There is room in front of you. A small touch can take you into it.

steps.desc: Turn with the ball close. You can look up again as you move.
steps.say: Turn with the ball close. You can look up again as you move.

steps.desc: Send it back and try another picture. Watch how the defender changes position.
steps.say: Send it back and try another picture. Watch how the defender changes position.

steps.desc: Check back toward the passer. This time the defender follows you.
steps.say: Check back toward the passer. This time the defender follows you.

steps.desc: Receive with the defender close in front. You still have help behind.
steps.say: Receive with the defender close in front. You still have help behind.

steps.desc: You do not have to turn every time. Keep the ball away from pressure.
steps.say: You do not have to turn every time. Keep the ball away from pressure.

steps.desc: Give it back. You kept possession because you noticed the pressure.
steps.say: Give it back. You kept possession because you noticed the pressure.

steps.desc: The defender takes the return away from pressure. The midfielder moves to offer another angle instead of staying beside the opponent.
steps.say: The defender takes the return away from pressure. The midfielder moves to offer another angle instead of staying beside the opponent.

catalog.name: Look, Then Turn or Return
catalog.what: Look for pressure before receiving. Turn into room or give the ball back.
catalog.coach: Before the pass arrives, look over your shoulder. Where is the defender?

questions.q: Which choice uses the room ahead to gain ground?
questions.explain: The defender is off to the side. You have room to turn and move forward.

paths.why: You can move forward without entering the defender’s space.
A return is available, but you can gain ground here.

choiceExplanations: You can move forward without entering the defender’s space.
A return is available, but you can gain ground here.

questions.q: Is there room to turn forward, or do you need to return the ball?
questions.explain: The defender blocks the turn now. Your teammate behind is free.

paths.why: This touch takes you toward the defender.
The return pass keeps the ball and gives you time to move again.

choiceExplanations: This touch takes you toward the defender.
The return pass keeps the ball and gives you time to move again.

questions.q: True or false? You look for the defender before the pass arrives.
questions.explain: Yes. Looking early tells you if you can turn.
choiceExplanations: Yes. Looking early tells you if you can turn.
Look before the ball comes, so you already know where the defender is.

questions.q: You get the ball with room ahead. Put the steps in order.
options: Dribble ahead with your head up
questions.explain: Right. Look first, receive open, turn, then dribble ahead.
choiceExplanations: Right. Look first, receive open, turn, then dribble ahead.
Receive after you have looked, so you know where the defender is.
Turn only once the ball is at your feet.
Dribble ahead last, once you have turned into the room.

questions.q: The defender is far away this time. What do you do?
questions.explain: Yes. The defender is far, so you can turn into the room.
choiceExplanations: There is room ahead, so passing straight back wastes a chance to move forward.
Yes. The defender is far, so you can turn into the room.
Waiting lets the defender run back and close you down.

questions.q: There is room ahead. What should your first touch do?
options: Small touch into the room ahead
Big kick far ahead, then chase
Stop it dead and look down
questions.explain: Yes. A small touch keeps the ball close, so you can turn into the room.
choiceExplanations: Yes. A small touch keeps the ball close, so you can turn into the room.
A big touch runs away from you, so the defender can win it.
Looking down at a stopped ball wastes the room, so the defender closes in.

name: Carry or Pass?
concept: Watch which route the defender leaves open.
desc: Watch which route the defender leaves open.

steps.desc: Your teammate is to the right. Watch the defender between you.
steps.say: Your teammate is to the right. Watch the defender between you.

steps.desc: The defender is staying in the passing lane. Look at the grass ahead.
steps.say: The defender is staying in the passing lane. Look at the grass ahead.

steps.desc: Carry into the space. Keep the ball close enough to change your mind.
steps.say: Carry into the space. Keep the ball close enough to change your mind.

steps.desc: The defender comes across to stop you. Your teammate has room now.
steps.say: The defender comes across to stop you. Your teammate has room now.

steps.desc: Look up before you run into the defender. You have another way forward.
steps.say: Look up before you run into the defender. You have another way forward.

steps.desc: Pass to your teammate. Your carry made the defender choose.
steps.say: Pass to your teammate. Your carry made the defender choose.

catalog.name: Carry or Pass?
catalog.what: Watch which route the defender leaves open.
catalog.coach: Your teammate is to the right. Watch the defender between you.

questions.q: Which route would you choose?
questions.explain: The pass is covered, but you can move forward with the ball.

paths.why: There is room to carry before the defender can get across.
The defender stands in this passing lane.

choiceExplanations: There is room to carry before the defender can get across.
The defender stands in this passing lane.

questions.q: Which route would you choose?
questions.explain: The defender has closed your running route. The pass to the right is open.

paths.why: The defender is directly ahead.
The defender has left this passing lane.

choiceExplanations: The defender is directly ahead.
The defender has left this passing lane.

questions.q: Which picture shows it is time to pass right?
questions.explain: Yes. The defender came across to you, so the passing lane is open.
choiceExplanations: The defender is in the passing lane, so the pass could be cut out.
Yes. The defender came across to you, so the passing lane is open.
The defender is next to your teammate, so a pass there is not safe.

questions.q: You carried forward. What will the defender do next?
questions.explain: Yes. Your carry pulls the defender to you, so the lane opens.
choiceExplanations: Yes. Your carry pulls the defender to you, so the lane opens.
Then you could run free at goal, so the defender must come to you.
Running away gives you room to shoot, so the defender steps toward you.

questions.q: Now the defender is in front of you. Which pass is open?
questions.explain: Yes. The defender stands in front, so the right lane is open.
choiceExplanations: The defender is right in that lane, so the pass could be cut out.
Yes. The defender stands in front, so the right lane is open.

name: Make Room for Your Team
concept: Spread into useful space so the player on the ball has another route.
desc: Spread into useful space so the player on the ball has another route.

steps.desc: The left teammate is close to the defender. There is more room near the side.
steps.say: The left teammate is close to the defender. There is more room near the side.

steps.desc: A wider position can open a new passing angle. Keep watching the ball.
steps.say: A wider position can open a new passing angle. Keep watching the ball.

steps.desc: Move wider while the defender holds the old lane.
steps.say: Move wider while the defender holds the old lane.

steps.desc: The pass can reach the wide teammate. The team has more room to play.
steps.say: The pass can reach the wide teammate. The team has more room to play.

steps.desc: Give it back. The defender starts moving toward that left side.
steps.say: Give it back. The defender starts moving toward that left side.

steps.desc: Look across the field. There is room for a teammate on the other side.
steps.say: Look across the field. There is room for a teammate on the other side.

steps.desc: The right teammate moves wide. You do not all need to gather around the ball.
steps.say: The right teammate moves wide. You do not all need to gather around the ball.

steps.desc: Pass into that room. Width helped because it changed the passing angle.
steps.say: Pass into that room. Width helped because it changed the passing angle.

steps.desc: After passing wide, the middle midfielder moves across behind the ball to offer a return angle.
steps.say: After passing wide, the middle midfielder moves across behind the ball to offer a return angle.

catalog.name: Make Room for Your Team
catalog.what: Spread into useful space so the player on the ball has another route.
catalog.coach: The left teammate is close to the defender. There is more room near the side.

questions.q: Where could the left teammate move to help?
questions.explain: Moving wider takes the receiver away from the blocked lane.

spots.why: The defender cannot cover this wider route from the same position.
This puts you close to the passer without opening the left route.

choiceExplanations: The defender cannot cover this wider route from the same position.
This puts you close to the passer without opening the left route.

questions.q: Where would another supporting run help most?
questions.explain: The defender followed the left route. A wide right option gives the passer a different way out.

spots.why: The defender is already close to this space.
The far side has room for a new passing angle.

choiceExplanations: The defender is already close to this space.
The far side has room for a new passing angle.

questions.q: True or false? Everyone should gather close around the ball.
questions.explain: Right, it's false. Spreading out gives the passer more routes.
choiceExplanations: Crowding the ball lets one defender block every pass.
Right, it's false. Spreading out gives the passer more routes.

questions.q: The defender moved to the left side. Which pass is open now?
questions.explain: Yes. Your right teammate moved wide into open room.
choiceExplanations: Yes. Your right teammate moved wide into open room.
The defender moved toward that side, so the pass could be cut out.

questions.q: The right teammate is close to a defender. Where should they move?
questions.explain: Yes. Wide on the right opens a new passing angle.
choiceExplanations: Moving to the ball crowds the space, so one defender can block both.
The blue player is in that lane, so the pass could be cut out.
Yes. Wide on the right opens a new passing angle.

name: Step Out of the Blocked Lane
concept: Move so the defender is no longer between you and the ball.
desc: Move so the defender is no longer between you and the ball.

steps.desc: The defender stands between the passer and the left teammate.
steps.say: The defender stands between the passer and the left teammate.

steps.desc: The left teammate can change the angle instead of waiting behind the defender.
steps.say: The left teammate can change the angle instead of waiting behind the defender.

steps.desc: Step diagonally away from the blocked lane. Show the passer where you are.
steps.say: Step diagonally away from the blocked lane. Show the passer where you are.

steps.desc: The pass reaches you through the new angle.
steps.say: The pass reaches you through the new angle.

steps.desc: Return the ball while the lane is still clear.
steps.say: Return the ball while the lane is still clear.

steps.desc: The defender shifts across to cover the left pass. Check the other teammate.
steps.say: The defender shifts across to cover the left pass. Check the other teammate.

steps.desc: One option is covered, but the right teammate can still help.
steps.say: One option is covered, but the right teammate can still help.

steps.desc: Pass right, then make a useful return angle.
steps.say: Pass right, then make a useful return angle.

catalog.name: Step Out of the Blocked Lane
catalog.what: Move so the defender is no longer between you and the ball.
catalog.coach: The defender stands between the passer and the left teammate.

questions.q: Where could the left teammate offer a clear pass?
questions.explain: The diagonal move takes the receiver out of this blocked lane.

spots.why: The new angle goes around the defender.
The defender is still between you and the ball.

choiceExplanations: The new angle goes around the defender.
The defender is still between you and the ball.

questions.q: Which teammate has the clear forward passing lane?
questions.explain: The defender moved into the left lane. The right lane is open.

paths.why: The defender now covers this route.
The defender cannot cover both routes from there.

choiceExplanations: The defender now covers this route.
The defender cannot cover both routes from there.

questions.q: True or false? The defender blocks the pass to the left teammate.
questions.explain: Right, it's true. The defender stands right in the line of that pass.
choiceExplanations: Right, it's true. The defender stands right in the line of that pass.
Look at the line from the ball. The defender stands right in the way.

questions.q: Which picture gives the left teammate a clear lane?
options: Left teammate steps forward and out
questions.explain: Yes. Stepping on a slant moves you out of the defender's lane, so the pass is open.
choiceExplanations: You are still straight behind the defender, so the pass is blocked.
Waiting behind the defender keeps the lane blocked, so the pass can't reach you.
Yes. Stepping on a slant moves you out of the defender's lane, so the pass is open.

questions.q: Now the defender blocks the right teammate. Which pass is open?
questions.explain: Yes. The defender moved right, so the lane to the left teammate is clear.
choiceExplanations: The defender stands in that lane now, so the pass could be stolen.
Yes. The defender moved right, so the lane to the left teammate is clear.
